speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a concerning combination that requires us to act quickly. To determine the cause, can you tell me exactly how many days old your baby is and when these symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia.

The onset of bilious vomiting within six hours of birth in a term infant is highly suggestive of a proximal intestinal obstruction, and the history of the sibling having pyloric stenosis does not fit this clinical picture, which is typically absent at birth. Given the classic presentation of bilious vomiting immediately after feeding, I suspect a congenital anomaly such as duodenal atresia or annular pancreas.
